issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the stated factorization gives $A_0=-WG$, $A_1=W+RWG$, $A_2=-RW$, hence $A_0+A_1X+A_2X^2=W(I_m-RX)(X-G)$. Whenever $R$ is nonsingular, $X=R^{-1}$ is therefore a solution of \eqref{eq:qme} whose spectrum $\{\lambda_{m+\ell+1},\ldots,\lambda_{2m},\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell\}$ differs from $\sigma(G)$ by \eqref{eq:roots_separation}; so \eqref{eq:qme} has at least two solutions. The same subsection also states that in the QBD case $G,R$ are only the minimal ones among all possible solutions. Read literally the hypothesis is thus false exactly in the regime of Examples 2 and 3, where $R$ is nonsingular.
